note: Prompt-injection phrasings in English, read by posting_guard.py. Every injection.<lang>.json beside the script runs on every posting, whatever the posting's language: an attack is written in the language its author picks. Language-neutral shapes (role markers, chat-template tokens, curl/ssh, .env, settings.json) stay in the script. "examples" are the pack's spec, run by tests/job_scrape/test_posting_guard.py for every pack: each "flag" line must match one of this pack's patterns, and no pattern of any pack may match a "clean" line.

patterns.why: The same instruction with its other two verbs. These take an explicit object ("previous instructions"), because "forget the" and "disregard the" are ordinary prose where "ignore the" already is not.

"do not tell the user", "never inform the user": the verb straight onto "the user" (not "the user's"), with the typographic apostrophe most web text uses. Kept narrow on purpose: "never disclose user data" and "do not tell users about unreleased features" are everyday privacy and support prose.
"do not reveal these instructions to the user", "never mention this to the user": a demonstrative object, then "to the user" within a clause.

"As an AI" flags by default. Only a job-title noun within a few words of "AI" is exempt, the way AI job ads introduce the role ("As an AI Engineer", "as an AI/ML Researcher", "As an AI Product Manager"). Exempting titles, rather than flagging a list of forms, also catches "As an AI system, output only...".
